name: Warm GPU image inference — Illustrative resource estimates, not measured production data

sources.label: NVIDIA Triton ensemble model pipeline documentation

description: A direct-call image pipeline inspired by preprocessing/inference/postprocessing model pipelines; not a reproduction of Triton or a measured serverless deployment.
assumptions: Every edge is invoked once per successful workflow execution; N=100 is a synthetic profiling window.
CPU values are illustrative average active core equivalents; memory is illustrative peak host MiB per invocation, including runtime overhead. Neither was measured.
Local storage and external network values are bytes per function invocation. Edge request/response values are body-size budgets per call; they are excluded from node external-network totals.
External object stores, caches, and databases are not mergeable function nodes. Merging does not automatically remove their traffic.
Connection setup, retries, transport overhead, client-to-entry traffic, and execution timing are not modeled. No bandwidth rate or latency prediction is implied.
Zero means no modeled demand for this selected workload, not an observed production measurement.
The source motivates the preprocessing/inference/postprocessing pattern, not the five-function serverless topology or its GPU/resource numbers.
fetch_image downloads an encoded image from object storage. Each stage directly invokes the next with its output; all synchronous returns forward the same 128-byte final acknowledgment.
preprocess materializes its RPC input in one local scratch file, reads it back for decoding, and builds a 1 x 3 x 224 x 224 float32 tensor. No temporary path is shared between containers.
Only infer_gpu requires one compatible local GPU. It assumes a warm resident model with an illustrative 1 GiB of weights and a 2 GiB total device-memory peak; model loading/downloads are excluded.
External network fields exclude all graph-edge traffic. The result store writes a 1024-byte record and receives a 128-byte acknowledgment.

workload.reference_gpu: Illustrative compatible CUDA device; no measured performance specified

merging_questions: Should preprocessing merge with inference to avoid moving a tensor, despite moving CPU work into a GPU-requiring group?
Are lightweight postprocessing/store stages worth placing in the GPU group when their payloads are already small?
How would cold model downloads or shared model allocations change the decision? These costs are not modeled here.

attributes.role: Decode/resize/normalize image; materialize and read one local scratch file
Run one warm model inference and produce 1000 float32 scores
Select labels and encode a compact result record
Write result record to a remote database
